text:
tor: Heads-up 10 -- large broker asked for an on-prem "airlock" deployment. They want clarity on three things: install path (operator vs offline bundle + local registry mirror), upgrade windows & SLA for patches, and commercial model for offline entitlements.

nicole: They also asked about signing key custody: do we hold signing keys or can customers bring their own (BYOK) for bundle signing? And what's the cert rotation timeline?

ben: Quick answers: we support operator installs and fully immutable bundles. For strict air-gapped installs we recommend providing a local container registry mirror that we populate in the bundle (images + manifests). We can also deliver an offline registry tar that the customer loads into their mirror.

frank: On signing: standard is Redwood-signed artifacts. For enterprise deals we offer an option for customer-assisted signing where we deliver artifacts and a signing tool; customer runs signing in their KMS/HSM and returns a signed bundle. BYOK requires an Addendum in the contract.

nicole: Good to note: cert/key rotation cadence we recommend is 90 days for short-lived activation keys and 12 months for signing keys by default. We provide a cert-rotation guide and automation scripts as part of the offline-support SOW.

tor: Upgrade cadence question from buyer: they want predictable windows and a freeze period during month-end trading. Can we guarantee no upgrades in certain blackout windows?

ben: Yes. We support locked-upgrade schedules per customer: e.g., quarterly upgrades only, with emergency hotfixes outside the window for CVEs. We will encode blackout windows in the rollout policy and respect them during upgrade planning.

support-bot: support-bot: delivery-modes: monthly-security, quarterly-feature, emergency-hotfix. Rollout-respect-blackouts: true (when contractually agreed).

nicole: Pricing model: base on-prem license (per logical cluster) + offline-entitlement fee (one-time packaging + yearly support) + per-node runtime licensing if they want pay-per-node. Suggest we offer two commercial options in proposal: 1) cluster license + annual offline SOW; 2) node-based license with included 12-month offline support.

frank: Also raise export control check: if customer wants FIPS/HSM integration, note which cryptography modules are covered and if we need a specific build. Might be a separate compliance SOW.

tor: Buyer also asked about validation test harness they can run in air-gapped env to smoke the install and perf. Do we have something?

ben: We include a small test harness in the bundle: smoke scripts (k8s manifests + synthetic load), health checks, and a validation report template. For regulated customers we can run a pre-signed validation run and provide a signed report (fee-based).

nicole: Ops detail: rollback path is apply previous signed bundle digest and run the contained rollback script. We include a recommended rollback window and a checklist in the bundle README.

tor: Action items: ben to prepare offline-registry + mirror instructions and the validation harness snippet; nicole to draft two pricing scenarios and the BYOK addendum language; frank to list compliance build flags and estimated SOW hours for cert rotation and FIPS/HSM work. We need a response to buyer within 48 hours.

ben: Heres the mirror/load snippet we hand ops:
```
# load registry mirror from offline bundle
mkdir -p /var/tmp/redwood-mirror
tar -xzvf redwood-registry-mirror-2026.tgz -C /var/tmp/redwood-mirror
skopeo copy --dest-tls-verify=false --insecure-policy \
  dir:/var/tmp/redwood-mirror/docker-archive docker://localhost:5000
```

frank: Noted timeline risk: BYOK and HSM integrations typically add 2-4 weeks to onboarding due to security reviews. Flag that in the response.

tor: Great. If no objections, stitch this into a short answer doc and commercial options, then send. :thumbsup:
